label: TRENDnet TPE-TG50g
description: TRENDnet TPE-TG50g (v4) - five-port unmanaged gigabit desktop switch with PoE+ on four ports: 4x 10/100/1000 PoE/PoE+ RJ45 at up to 30 W each against a 31 W total budget, 1x plain gigabit RJ45 for the uplink, 10 Gbps switching capacity, fanless, 54 V DC 0.7 A external adapter.

poe.note: PoE standard 802.3af/at, Mode A (pins 1, 2, 3 and 6 carry power), ports 1-4 only, up to 30 W per port, 31 W total budget. The budget binds long before the port count: one 30 W 802.3at device fills it, two 15.4 W 802.3af devices fit (30.8 W), and four powered devices only fit at Class 2 (7 W) draw each. Port 5 is data only, so a fifth powered device on this box is a cabling error the spec should refuse. Full PoE load is stated at 33.4 W input, 3.1 W with no PoE load.

fabric.note: Vendor switch fabric of 10 Gbps for five gigabit ports (5 x 2 Gbps full duplex), matching the 7.44 Mpps forwarding rate.

notes: TRENDnet TPE-TG50g v4 figures from the product page (https://www.trendnet.com/products/PoE/5-Port-Gigabit-PoEplus-Switch-TPE-TG50g-v4). Hardware: 4x 10/100/1000 PoE+ ports and 1x 10/100/1000 port, all Auto-MDIX, 128 KB packet buffer, 2K MAC entries, 7.44 Mpps forwarding, 9 KB jumbo frames, IEEE 802.3/802.3u/802.3x/802.3ab/802.3af/802.3at/802.3az, fanless metal case 105 x 98 x 28 mm, 276 g, external 54 V DC 0.7 A adapter, 3.1 W no-load and 33.4 W at full PoE load, 0-40 C. Unmanaged: no CLI, no HTTP server, no VLANs. This is the smallest member of the family and its 31 W budget cannot power four PoE+ devices at once.
